steps.content: [Cavendish Residence]

The two candidates sit across from each other, with Councilor Cavendish letting the butler serve tea to the guest. Sunlight streams in through the windows, casting a warm glow over the room. She leisurely sips her tea, her gaze fixed on the man seated opposite her.
Then, a smile of sympathy graces her face.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I know you are up against a formidable enemy. This recent assault is particularly devastating—a coordinated strike almost from every corner. It seems they've timed this moment to break you entirely.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Quite overwhelming, isn't it? You may have been a seasoned businessman, but when it comes to politics, you're practically an amateur, still figuring out the playbook.
She delicately sets her teacup down and locks eyes with Max King, exuding perfect composure.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: To be frank, I admire what you bring to the table. DisCity is approaching a critical turning point, and you could very well be an exceptional leader. This city needs someone like you—and if there's anything you need, I can help.
Her kind gesture, however, receives no friendly response. Max King leaves the teacup untouched, fixing his opponent with an icy stare.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Drop the act. Your attempts to undermine me are just stepping stones for your own power grab. Normally, I wouldn’t concern myself with your scheming. I'd just fight you to the bitter end.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: But you've crossed the line this time. How could you stoop so low as to get Adrian involved and use him to threaten me?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I had respect for you. Your niece made a real impact in the West District, and you, yourself, also displayed integrity. You didn't hesitate to speak up when Stewart was knee-deep in his shady dealings.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: For a person of your stature to side with special interests is one thing, but to stoop to those underhanded tricks? Do you have no shame, Councilor Cavendish?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: You're insinuating that I orchestrated these schemes against you... Show me your evidence?
Her calm words instantly ignite his fury.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Evidence?! That evidence will find its way to court soon. I am here to appeal to whatever conscience you've got left!

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Heh, you seem to have misunderstood. I'm just expressing my surprise.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: It's quite astonishing that even with your life on the line, you still fail to identify your real enemy, instead wasting your precious time on me.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...What do you mean?
[Mood shifts]

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: For now, I'm on the stage just the same as David Stewart was. We're both handpicked "representatives" pushed into the limelight.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: He was the perfect choice. With no political allies of his own, he had to pledge absolute loyalty to the powers to secure his position. This explains his fervent dedication and radical stance—qualities that made him a far more fitting representative than I.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Had he lived, his backers would have ensured his re-election regardless of his waning popularity. Unfortunately, his untimely passing left them in a scramble to find a fitting replacement in time.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: So, between you and I, they had to settle for the lesser evil. Your presence actually cast me in a more favorable light in their eyes. And well, here we are.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Getting rid of you is someone else's job. I'm just here to siphon away your votes. They don't need me to get my hands dirty—I have to maintain a clean image.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Save your excuses. You've all had your fill of backroom deals and power plays. This election is meant to change everything. It's not your private little game anymore. The next leader will be chosen by millions of DisCitizens.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: That's hardly fair. If the common people have the right to choose, shouldn't the elite also be entitled to that same privilege?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Everyone simply votes for the one who aligns with their interests. You're a champion of the common folk, riding the waves of change with your band of idealists. You want to reshape the city, redistribute resources, and benefit the masses—that is indeed admirable.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: "Unite all who desire change"—when you choose this slogan, you should've known what kind of allies you were seeking, and what kind of enemies you were making.
Though equally seated on the sofa, Bernadette's demeanor looms over her political rival as if she is gazing down upon him from a higher vantage point.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: By siding with the powerless to take the pie from the powerful, you should have been ready, and you should have thought things through—what others are capable of, and how they will strike back.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: That right-hand man of yours understands this far better than you do.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: That's why while you keep picking fights and making enemies, he has no choice but to work tirelessly building your defenses—even if it means seeking help from the Outlands.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...You mean Adrian?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Adrian would never collude with the Outlands. He has no reason to! I know him better than anyone. Don't you dare slander him to my face.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I am complimenting him. Mr. Vale seems to be the only clear-headed person in your naive little campaign team. Surely you didn't think your modest fortune alone could sustain an election campaign?
With a faint smile, Bernadette gestures for her butler to refill Max King's tea.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Running for election needs money, but all legitimate major fundraising channels have closed their doors to you. Your personal wealth? Please. Not even ten fortunes like yours could cover it. How else could he finance your grand crusade without finding alternative means?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Truly, against a retired veteran with ties to Syndicate like him, concocting an accusation would be child's play. They could pin anything on him—extortion, smuggling, bribery. The prosecutors opted for the Outlands part simply because it would sell better in the news.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: And the public opinion you've built your triumph on? Even more susceptible to manipulation. A mere handful of media outlets, the reiteration of select narratives... and your standing could collapse in a single night.
Max King meets her words with palpable contempt.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Extortion, smuggling, bribery... Was that why you took Adrian away? For these charges?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: No way. The Adrian I know is the most upright person, an FAC veteran with a rock-solid conviction like no other. He supports me because he believes in my vision to change this city for the better.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Sure, he has ties to Syndicate, so what? The suffering in the West District, the shadows over our city—it's all your doing. But Adrian, like me, sees a path to change. Change that's already happening. He's got more honor than any of you, so don't you dare play your usual dirty games with him.

His words ring with indignation, yet the uncertainty in his expression already betrays his true feelings, and Bernadette finds it almost amusing.
—He doesn't even understand his own right-hand man, let alone grasp the true reasons behind his rise to prominence.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Eastside isn't buzzing because your people believe your ideals. It's stirred up because this election makes for good headlines—and a handful of media channels are all it takes.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Mr. Vale is acutely aware of all this. If it were you in custody, he'd be here this very moment, pleading on his knees, willing to sacrifice anything and everything just to convince me to release you.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: That's the difference between you two, Mr. King—experience. Now, what are you going to do?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Pin your hopes on your supposed new friend, that MBCC Chief? Indeed, he's someone who can be easily persuaded.
steps.female_content: Pin your hopes on your supposed new friend, that MBCC Chief? Indeed, she's someone who can be easily persuaded.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...So you admit it, huh? Finally owning up to your own doing?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: That so-called "protection request" you made with Chief? I bet you couldn’t care less about that girl’s life or what Chief thinks. Your only aim is to manipulate him into stepping in, just so you can leverage his influence through the media.
steps.female_content: That so-called "protection request" you made with Chief? I bet you couldn’t care less about that girl’s life or what Chief thinks. Your only aim is to manipulate her into stepping in, just so you can leverage her influence through the media.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: But you're wrong. He's a man that can never be swayed easily—he's in this for his own principles, protecting those he believes worthy of protection. He will expose your schemes, and never stoop to your level.
steps.female_content: But you're wrong. She's a woman that can never be swayed easily—she's in this for her own principles, protecting those she believes worthy of protection. She will expose your schemes, and never stoop to your level.

steps.content: A meaningful smile graces Bernadette's face.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Will he really?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Or let me rephrase this... Do you really want him to do that?
steps.female_content: Or let me rephrase this... Do you really want her to do that?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: At the moment, this so-called "protection request" is nothing more than hearsay and could still be considered part of his duties. People are eager to find out everyone's stance on the election, but nothing is certain yet. However, if he issues a formal denial, it would be seen as publicly supporting your candidacy.
steps.female_content: At the moment, this so-called "protection request" is nothing more than hearsay and could still be considered part of her duties. People are eager to find out everyone's stance on the election, but nothing is certain yet. However, if she issues a formal denial, it would be seen as publicly supporting your candidacy.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: As for the repercussions? Just look at the FAC now. See what happens to those with military power who dare to meddle in politics.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: That Chief only has what little freedom he does, thanks to his excessive prudence. But, if you plead for his help, he might sacrifice his own interests for yours, given his nature.
steps.female_content: That Chief only has what little freedom she does, thanks to her excessive prudence. But, if you plead for her help, she might sacrifice her own interests for yours, given her nature.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: If you can really do that, Mr. Vale would be very proud.
That Minos Chief did say something similar before.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Honestly, I know nothing about the election, nor do I want to. That position has never seemed to make any difference in the things I truly care about. If it really holds the value you say...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then please win and prove yourself by making real changes. Who knows? By then, I might be the one not letting you go.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Hmph... I'm not that desperate.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I don't need anyone making sacrifices for me, especially not my friends.
After a moment of silence, he asks in a low voice.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Did you kill Stewart?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I have better means to get what I want.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: To be honest, I'm not afraid of your means or whoever's behind you. But fine, you've won this round—I'm not sophisticated enough to throw my allies under the bus for my own victory.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Tell me straight. What's the deal to set Adrian free? Do you want me to quit the election?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I've already let him go.
Max King freezes in shock.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Wh... what are you really up to? Where is he?

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: As I've said, I'm not here to stand against you. I genuinely admire you, which means I could be an option for you.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I will speak with those behind me. When you return, you should also have a serious conversation with Mr. Vale.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: After all, it's your internal problems that are truly fatal. Your ideals were what forced him down this path.
(Scene change)
After leaving the Cavendish residence, Max King does not get into his car; he just walks mechanically, his movements rigid and robotic, hardly preserving the impeccable state of his suit.
He loses track of time, only to suddenly realize he's standing at the door of his campaign office. And there, right before him, stands...

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Adrian!!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Thank goodness... You really came back. I was even thinking about—
The elderly man stands in the doorway, his eyes sunken from what must be days without sleep. In a rare departure from his usual demeanor, he interrupts his young master.

steps.speaker: Vale
steps.content: ...Sir, the lawsuit has been settled. For the sake of your campaign, please cut connections with me. That way, I can make amends for the damage I've caused and make up for my mistakes.

steps.speaker: Vale
steps.content: I have faith in your victory, sir. Your growth and strength are evident, and you now have a more helpful hand by your side. As long as you persist without wavering, success will undoubtedly be yours.
Max King falters for a moment, his eyes filled with confusion.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: "Cut connections with you... A more helpful hand?" What are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: You want me to beg for Chief ${PlayerName}'s help—just so you can make your exit?
After those words, Max King feels a pang of regret. His hands clench tightly, as if trying to hold onto something slipping away.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: No, Adrian... Please don't go. You're my closest friend and most trusted ally. I will always trust you, no matter what comes our way.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: So please, trust in me too. I won't lose to someone like that.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Cavendish thinks she has intimidated me, but she's also exposed her hand. Those high-and-mighty jerks think they can manipulate everyone as they please, and they dare use you to threaten me? To hell with them!

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: In three days, I'll clear our names of every false accusation they've thrown at us at the rally. You'll see...

steps.speaker: Vale
steps.content: Max...

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Times have changed, and justice is now on my side...
[Scene Change] Cavendish Residence
Bernadette stands by the window, gazing into the distance. Earlier that day, she received her rival in this very room.
Now that he's gone, Bernadette finds herself dwelling on his words.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Thank you for your generous enlightenment. I'll definitely bear in mind those "unseen voters" behind you, now that I've learned what they're made of.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: But I have no reason to back down, absolutely none. You're the ones who should fear.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: The West District has become an undeniable force. The fact that your backers are resorting to every possible means of suppression only proves their own fear. You're all shaking in your boots at this new power, 'cause you know Syndicans will never vote for you.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: A new era is coming, and all you old timers will be left in the dust. Just you wait.
To think an amateur like him has made it to the finals... Should I blame David for dying too early, or...
The times really ARE changing...

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: He's right. It's only a matter of time... If I were a Syndican, I would choose him too.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Now... what should I do to satisfy those who've chosen me?
She opens a box and takes out a stick of incense, contemplating it briefly before breaking into a smile and putting it away.
...That's enough for today. It's time to rest.
[Scene Change] Shadow Protocol

- That MK handled yet? He didn't quit. Looks like he's still putting up a fight. - Whether he withdraws or not, it doesn't matter now. The public is turning against him. He doesn't stand a chance. That man's still too naive, he'll never make it to the stage. - Cavendish will win. Just focus on the West District in the next four years.

- By the way, any news on that Minos Chief? - All missions have failed. Someone's protecting him, making things hard. He's getting bolder lately, only to cause us more trouble. - Get it done, then. We've got hands in the EDGE to handle the fallout with Paradeisos.
steps.female_content: - By the way, any news on that Minos Chief? - All missions have failed. Someone's protecting her, making things hard. She's getting bolder lately, only to cause us more trouble. - Get it done, then. We've got hands in the EDGE to handle the fallout with Paradeisos.

steps.content: - Get it done? - Why get our own hands dirty? - I know just the right person. Let's have his "protectors" do some work. After all, that Chief loves poking his nose around, doesn't he?
steps.female_content: - Get it done? - Why get our own hands dirty? - I know just the right person. Let's have her "protectors" do some work. After all, that Chief loves poking her nose around, doesn't she?

steps.content: ${PlayerName} has fallen asleep at his desk. Jelena's coat lies draped over his shoulders, and the scattered documents on the desk have all been neatly arranged.
steps.female_content: ${PlayerName} has fallen asleep at her desk. Jelena's coat lies draped over her shoulders, and the scattered documents on the desk have all been neatly arranged.

steps.content: All the documents are the FAC operation reports during the election season, while the top two files mark the locations of bases that were recently attacked but never officially reported.
